chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) has some chosen ones among His creation whom He spares from afflictions; He keeps them alive in well-being, sustains them in well-being, causes them to die in well-being, resurrects them in well-being, and admits them into Paradise in well-being.

key_terms.ضَنَائِنَ: Chosen ones or those held dear by God
key_terms.عَافِيَةٍ: Well-being, health, and freedom from defect or harm
key_terms.يَضُنُّ بِهِمْ: He spares or protects them (from evil)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a believer to be spared from affliction in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (a.s.) explains that Allah has specific chosen servants whom He protects from trials and afflictions. These individuals experience divine grace in every stage of their existence: life, sustenance, death, resurrection, and entry into Paradise, all characterized by 'afiyah' (well-being/wholeness).

en.muhajir-b-ali: 22. It has been reported by Abu Hamzah that

Abu Ja'far (a.s) said: Allah has some chosen ones amongst His creatures whom He spares from afflictions. He keeps them alive in well-being, sustains them in well-being, causes them to die in a state of well-being, shall resurrect them in well-being and admit them into Paradise in well-being.
